answer: An identity posts a bond tied to a hardware root key, so one bond cannot back two machines. A duplicate submission forfeits it. Each epoch a rotating auditor pool re-runs one task per identity and burns the stake on a mismatch. A thousand-clone farm needs a thousand distinct root keys and a thousand live bonds. The whisper of one duplicate becomes an echo across the pool, and no yarrow field of cheap identities survives a single re-run that costs real hardware.
